newsitem.title: SPAIN: Iberdrola -- shares harmed by other privatisations.
newsitem.headline: Iberdrola -- shares harmed by other privatisations.

text.p: Spanish utility Iberdrola is currently undervalued on the stock market, financial director Jose Luis Sampedro told Spanish financial daily Expansion.

"Privatisations in the energy sector harm (our shares) because there is a diversion of funds towards those companies. For this reason, Iberdrola is not valued as it should be, although in the past few days the shares have improved a lot," he said in an interview published on Monday.
At 0925 GMT, Iberdrola shares were up 10 pesetas to 1,790.
In April, the government's last 10 percent stake in Repsol was sold, and a stake of up to 33 percent in electricity firm Endesa is due to come to the market in the autumn.

Around 30 percent of Iberdrola is held by foreign investors, with 12 percent in the U.S. and 18 percent in Europe, with the presence of institutional investors in the firm's capital seen increasing, Sampedro said.
He said Iberdrola's debt position is at present "comfortable," having fallen to around 840 billion pesetas.
Investments are being directed to improving installations, and so far this year the firm has also destined 10 billion pesetas to investment in Latin America, Sampedro said.
The firm has 75 percent of its debt in pesetas, and the remainder split between marks, Swiss francs and yen. Iberdrola is transferring all of its debt into pesetas, he added.
